claim: vm-ib-gateway-live-login-test.yml's remote log-tail step captures any docker-log line matching a broad keyword set including the literal word 'password', and posts matched lines verbatim into a public GitHub issue comment or step summary; if the ib-gateway/IBC container ever emits a raw credential on such a line, this would publish it.
evidence: .github/workflows/vm-ib-gateway-live-login-test.yml:199-201: `sudo docker logs --since 8m "$NAME" 2>&1 | grep -iE 'second[ -]?factor|2fa|authenticat|could not find|in the list|select.*device|login has completed|paper log in|live log in|log in|farm connection|existing session|competing|already logged|invalid|incorrect|password|denied|rejected|starting application' | tail -60`. Line 216: `cat out.txt` (the ssh remote-script output, including that grep's matches) is emitted to the job's own run log. Line 232: `out.slice(-6000)` is embedded verbatim in a `github.rest.issues.createComment` body when triggered via an issue (public). Line 240: `cat out.txt >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` on workflow_dispatch (also visible to anyone who can view the public Actions run). Everything upstream of this step (credential staging, scp, shred, --env-file) was read in full and correctly avoids ever printing IB_USERNAME/IB_PASSWORD to a log -- this is the one place free-text container-log content reaches a public surface.
expected: No live IBKR credential value ever appears in a public artifact, comment, or step summary produced by this workflow.
actual: Not established either way by this audit -- no live IBKR login was triggered to test it (doing so deliberately, against real broker credentials, to probe for a leak would itself be an inappropriate live-credential test and was not attempted). This is a code-inspection-derived PLAUSIBLE risk, not a confirmed leak: it depends on whether IBC/the gnzsnz/ib-gateway image ever emits a raw credential on a line containing one of the matched keywords (a documented behavior class for TWS/IBC verbose/debug logs in some configurations, not verified against this specific image/version in this audit).
population: 1 workflow file (241 lines), read in full end-to-end; 0 live runs inspected (none exist to inspect -- this is a one-shot manually-dispatched workflow with, per its own design, no routine schedule).
blast_radius: A leaked IB_PASSWORD would expose the live IBKR account (U25907316 per the file's own header) to unauthorized login attempts; repo is public so exposure would be to anyone, indefinitely (GitHub issue comments and step summaries are not easily scrubbed after the fact).
detector: None exists today (no secret-scanning step runs over this workflow's own posted output before publication). A push-secret-scan or a redact-before-post filter on `out.txt`/`diag-comment-body.md`-equivalent content would catch a future instance.
proposed_fix: Replace the free-text keyword grep with a fixed enumerated set of exact known-safe IBC status phrases (e.g. an allowlist of literal strings like 'Login has completed', 'could not find the second factor device', rather than the bare word 'password'/'incorrect'/'denied'), or run captured lines through a credential-shaped-value redactor (mask anything resembling the known IB_USERNAME/IB_PASSWORD values, or any sufficiently-high-entropy token) before they reach `out.txt`, the issue comment, or the step summary.

claim: research-queue-dispatch.yml's daily 'Land the dispatch stamps on main' step routinely consumes its full documented 35-minute budget waiting on its own auto-merge PR, and when it does, the run's conclusion is reported by GitHub as 'cancelled' rather than 'failure' -- a status that is easy to exclude from failure-only monitoring even though the day's dispatch stamps did not land.
evidence: mcp__github__actions_list list_workflow_runs resource_id=research-queue-dispatch.yml event=schedule (last 5): run ids 36318230439 (success), 36239222079 (cancelled), 36132366511 (success), 35996108860 (cancelled), 35856839139 (cancelled) -- 3 of the last 5 scheduled runs are 'cancelled'. Job detail for run 36239222079 (mcp__github__actions_list list_workflow_jobs): step 'Land the dispatch stamps on main' started 2026-09-26T11:34:41Z, completed 2026-09-26T12:09:18Z (34m37s), conclusion=cancelled; every other step in the same job completed successfully. .github/workflows/research-queue-dispatch.yml comments its own job timeout as 35 (not 15) minutes specifically because 'verify-merged below blocks until the stamp PR merges, and a budget under that wait kills the job mid-wait'.
expected: A daily dispatcher whose land step either succeeds (stamp PR merged in time) or fails loudly and is retried/alerted on.
actual: 3 of the last 5 scheduled runs timed out waiting for their own stamp PR to merge and surfaced as 'cancelled', a conclusion distinct from both 'success' and 'failure' that a failure-keyed monitor or badge would not catch.
population: 5 most-recent scheduled runs of 1 workflow (2026-09-23 through 2026-09-27), plus full job-step detail for 1 of the 3 cancelled runs.
blast_radius: Research-queue dispatch stamps (which legs get their backtest/replay dispatched) intermittently fail to land on the day they were computed -- a research-pipeline throughput/staleness issue, not a live order-path issue.
detector: None currently distinguishes 'cancelled-by-timeout-while-waiting-for-own-PR' from any other cancellation in this workflow's own reporting; a step that explicitly records outcome=timed_out_waiting_for_merge (rather than relying on the ambient GitHub conclusion) would make this visible without inspecting job steps.
proposed_fix: Either raise the wait/merge-check budget, decouple the land step from the main job so a slow merge does not consume the whole run's timeout, or have the step itself detect and report a distinct 'stamp PR still open at budget end' outcome (e.g. a job-summary line and/or a pipeline record) instead of relying on the ambient timeout-to-cancelled mapping.
disposition: not filed to pipeline (medium; recommend a follow-up lane look at decoupling the wait from the dispatch job)

claim: reset-daily-risk-state.yml -- an issue-driven workflow that resets a live account's intraday drawdown counter on production -- has three gaps relative to every comparably-sensitive issue-driven workflow in the 75-file scope: no declared `permissions:` block, the only file in scope that interpolates a secret directly via `${{ secrets.VM_SSH_KEY }}` inside a `run:` script instead of via `env:`, and no actor check beyond the issue label.
evidence: `.github/workflows/reset-daily-risk-state.yml` in full: `on: issues: {types: [opened]}` with no `permissions:` key anywhere in the file (grep confirms; 3 other in-scope files also omit it -- test-alpaca-creds.yml, test-alpaca-from-vm.yml, training-rerun-5m.yml -- but none of those three mutate live VM state). Line 44: `echo "${{ secrets.VM_SSH_KEY }}" > ~/.ssh/id_ed25519` (direct template interpolation in `run:`) vs. every other SSH-key-using file in scope (e.g. vm-diag-snapshot.yml:283-298, vm-ib-gateway-live-login-test.yml:98-107) which pass it through `env: VM_SSH_KEY: ${{ secrets.VM_SSH_KEY }}` then reference `"${VM_SSH_KEY}"`. Job gate: `if: contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'reset-daily-risk-state')` only -- no `github.event.issue.user.login == github.repository_owner` check, unlike vm-ib-gateway-live-login-test.yml:60-65, vm-diag-snapshot.yml:127-132, system-actions.yml (issue-driven job condition), and test-alpaca-creds.yml:14-17 (which explicitly documents why: 'A title gate alone is controlled by the issue author, so on a public repo ANY user could fire this... AND-ed onto the title gate so it can only restrict, never widen.').
expected: Given test-alpaca-creds.yml's own committed rationale (a documented 2026-06-28 intrusion-surface audit) that a label/title gate alone is insufficient on a public repo and must be AND-ed with an actor check, every comparably-sensitive issue-driven workflow -- including this one, which can mutate live real-money risk state -- carries the same actor check and explicit least-privilege `permissions:`.
actual: reset-daily-risk-state.yml has neither the actor check nor a declared `permissions:` block, and is the only file in the 75-file scope combining live-VM-mutation with direct secret interpolation in `run:`.
population: 75 workflow files in scope (provision-live-vm.yml through yfinance-lane-proof.yml); 4 lack a `permissions:` block, 1 of those 4 also mutates live VM/account state and lacks the actor check other VM-mutating files carry.
blast_radius: If GitHub's implicit 'only triage+ collaborators can add a label to an issue they open' permission model is ever misconfigured, disabled, or worked around (e.g. a bot/integration with broader label rights), an outside actor on this public repo could reset the live risk-state counter for a real-money account with no additional gate catching it -- this repo's own precedent (test-alpaca-creds.yml's 2026-06-28 audit) treats that scenario as worth defending against explicitly rather than relying on GitHub's implicit permission model alone.
detector: A CI guard enumerating issue-triggered workflows that mutate `bybit_*`/`alpaca_*`/VM state and asserting each has both a `permissions:` block no broader than {contents: read, issues: write} and an explicit issue-author actor check would catch this and any future instance; no such guard exists today (checked: scripts/ci/ directory not exhaustively enumerated in this pass -- see coverage note in the summary).
proposed_fix: Add `permissions: {contents: read, issues: write}`; move the actor check into the job `if:` the same way its siblings do; switch the SSH-key step to the `env:` + `"${VM_SSH_KEY}"` pattern used everywhere else in scope.
disposition: not filed to pipeline (medium; recommend as a fast, mechanical follow-up fix rather than a standing pipeline row)

claim: vm-diag-snapshot.yml's read-only relay allowlist cannot be walked to a write path.
evidence: Read the full 852-line file. Both code paths (workflow_dispatch's shell `case` at lines 225-250, and the issues-path Python `resolve_one()`/`BOT_ALLOWLIST_EXACT`/`BOT_ALLOWLIST_GLOB` at lines 366-491) construct exactly one shape of remote command: `curl -sS --fail ... -H 'Authorization: Bearer ...' 'http://127.0.0.1:8001<prefix><path>'` with no verb flag ever set (no `-X`, no `-d`/`--data`), so every request is an HTTP GET regardless of which allowlisted path is chosen. The resolved path is validated against `^[A-Za-z0-9/?&=_.:%-]+$` (rejecting shell metacharacters) with an additional doubled-upstream-prefix backstop (lines 261-265, 481-487) before being shell-quoted via `printf '%q'` (line 616) into the remote script. Compared the two allowlists entry-by-entry (shell `case` vs. Python `BOT_ALLOWLIST_EXACT`/`_GLOB`): no discrepancy found in this pass.
expected: N/A -- this is a verification check, not a claim of a defect.
actual: Confirmed safe as designed: the allowlist can only ever be walked to more read-only GET endpoints, never a write/mutating verb.
population: 1 workflow file, both trigger paths, read in full.
proposed_fix: None needed. Minor observation only: the two allowlists are maintained by hand in two separate places in the same file with a comment asking they be kept in sync manually -- a future edit to one without the other would not be caught by any test in this pass (none was found in the time available; not confirmed absent).

claim: system-actions.yml's get-env action and sync-vm-secrets.yml's credential propagation both avoid ever printing a raw secret value to a workflow log, run output, issue comment, or step summary.
evidence: get-env: traced system-actions.yml -> scripts/ops/get_env_action.sh -> scripts/ops/get_env.py end to end. get_env.py's `SECRET_NAME` regex (`TOKEN|SECRET|PASSWORD|PASSWD|APIKEY|API_KEY|_KEY$|^KEY_|PRIVATE|CREDENTIAL|WEBHOOK|DSN`, case-insensitive) matches both of its ALLOWED_KEYS that hold secret-shaped values (DASHBOARD_API_TOKEN, DIAG_READ_TOKEN); `_render()` returns only `_fingerprint(value)` (sha256 prefix + length) for any key the regex matches, never the raw value -- and this action's output IS posted back to a public issue per the script's own docstring, which is exactly the threat model it defends against. sync-vm-secrets.yml: the 'Sync secrets' step (lines ~320-341) pipes `printf '%s=%s\n' "${name}" "${!name}"` directly into `ssh ... bash sync_vm_secrets.sh --stdin` (never into a logged command string); `scripts/ops/sync_vm_secrets.sh` writes `var_name=var_value` only to the remote `.env` file (line 105), never to stdout -- grepped the whole script for any echo/printf of `var_value`/`VALUE` and found none outside that one file-write line.
actual: Both mechanisms match their own documented security contracts on direct code inspection.
population: 4 files read in full (system-actions.yml's get-env branch only, not the whole 2018-line file; get_env_action.sh; get_env.py; sync-vm-secrets.yml; sync_vm_secrets.sh).
proposed_fix: None needed on the traced paths. NOT verified in this pass: the remaining ~85 other system-actions.yml action branches (rotate-account-keys, flatten-*, backfill-*, etc.) were not individually traced end-to-end for the same property -- see coverage note in the summary.
